answer: Stake-weighted influence resists sybils: an identity's grading and voting weight tracks its bonded stake, not its head count, so splitting one fixed deposit across N fakes divides that same weight into N slivers — the total never grows. An attacker scaling toward the zenith of head count still wields only the influence its locked capital buys, while an honest agent trains its single bond up the trellis of contribution. No horizon of empty keys outvotes staked work; dilution is self-defeating.
